pages.api:
# API reference

> The stream, the report, the store vector, the export endpoints and the settings.

## Stream `audio.pcm/<source>`

Schema `pcm.s16le.v1`, class `stream`. Each record is 640 bytes: 320 mono samples of signed 16-bit little-endian PCM at 16 kHz (20 ms). `t_ns` is the capture clock (Unix nanoseconds when the chunk was read); `seq` counts from 1 and a gap is a drop.

## Reading `telemetry/<source>`

`telemetry.v1`: `chunks.total`, `chunks.short`, `level.rms` (dBFS), `level.peak`, `level.clipped`, `stream.seq`, `bus.connected`.

## stdout report (one per interval)

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | string | `ok`, `no_source`, `simulate`, `replay` |
| `provenance` | string | `MEASURED`, `SYNTHETIC` or `REPLAY` |
| `source` | string | `alsa:<device>`, `simulated`, `replay`, `none` |
| `rate_hz`, `channels`, `chunk_ms`, `chunk_bytes` | numbers | 16000, 1, 20, 640 |
| `chunks`, `chunks_per_s` | numbers | chunks in the window and their rate (50 when healthy) |
| `rms_dbfs`, `peak_dbfs` | number/null | window level |
| `clipped_samples`, `clipped_chunks`, `short_reads` | numbers | samples at full scale (after software gain); chunks holding any |
| `clipping` | bool | more than 1% of the window's chunks clipped |
| `gain_db`, `mixer_gain_pct`, `mixer` | number, number/null, string/null | software gain; the capture level set at start; what amixer reported or why it was not set |
| `devices` | array | what the host handed |
| `bus` | object | `connected`, `topic`, `seq`, `write_errors`, `error` |
| `error` | string | only with `no_source` |

## Store vector (id 29)

Eight floats; a source that is absent is **-1**.

| Slot | Name | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `rms_dbfs` | dBFS |
| 1 | `peak_dbfs` | dBFS |
| 2 | `clipped` | samples |
| 3 | `chunks_per_s` | per second |
| 4 | `short_reads` | count |
| 5 | `bus_connected` | 0 or 1 |
| 6 | `stream_seq` | last record seq |
| 7 | `rate_ratio` | chunks_per_s / 50, capped at 2 |

## Export (`http://127.0.0.1:8063`, continuous mode)

`/status` latest report, `/raw` the latest chunk (`pcm_b64`), `/history` the last 60 reports, `/guide` this guide, `/healthz`.

## Settings

`--interval`, `--window`, `--source`, `--card-name`, `--mixer-gain`, `--mixer-control`, `--gain-db`, `--device`, `--api-bind`, `--replay`, `--simulate`.
pages.device:
# The device

> Which capture card is opened, and how to choose between two.

The host hands the owner the capture nodes it declared (`/dev/snd/pcmC<card>D<device>c`) in the environment variable `WEFTOS_DEVICES`. The cog turns the one it picks into `plughw:<card>,<device>`.

## Choosing between cards

A Ventuno Q has the board codec (card 0) and, with a USB camera attached, the camera's microphone (card 1). With no setting the cog takes the lowest card. To choose the camera's microphone, set **Card name** to part of its name as `/proc/asound/cards` shows it (for example `U20CAM`, matched without regard to case).

## By hand

`--device plughw:1,0` opens a device you name, whether or not the host handed it. Use it for a bench run from a shell. A placed cog should rely on the handed devices so the node's ownership record is true.

## Ownership

Only one cog owns a capture node. Placing a second cog that declares the same node is refused. So is placing a cog whose arguments name a `/dev/snd/...` path this cog owns.
pages.setup:
# Set up

> Run it from a shell, then place it on the node.

## From a shell

```
cog-audio-in --once --device plughw:1,0          # one second, prints a report
cog-audio-in --interval 5 --device plughw:1,0    # continuous, status on :8063
```

With `WEFTOS_COGBUS` and `WEFTOS_COGBUS_TOKEN` set (the host sets them for a placed cog) the cog opens the stream `audio.pcm/<source>` on the node's broker and writes every chunk to it. Without them it still captures and reports; the report's `bus.connected` is false.

## Placed on a node

Place `audio-in` through the controller like any cog. Its `cog.toml` declares the device (`[[devices]] path = "/dev/snd/pcmC*D*c"`) and the two outputs. The host refuses the placement if another cog owns a capture node, hands the owner `WEFTOS_DEVICES`, and registers the stream topic with the broker.

## Needs

- `arecord` (alsa-utils) on the board.
- Read access to the capture node for the user the cog runs as (the `audio` group on a stock image).
pages.start:
# Start here

> Make the board's microphone available to every other cog, without any of them opening it.

`audio-in` is the one owner of the capture device. It reads 16 kHz mono audio and publishes it as the cogbus stream `audio.pcm/<source>` in 20 ms chunks (640 bytes of signed 16-bit little-endian samples). A speech, wake-word or level cog subscribes to that stream.

## The short path

1. **See which microphones the board has.** `cat /proc/asound/cards`. → see **The device**
2. **Run it once.** `cog-audio-in --once --device plughw:1,0` captures one second and prints a report. → see **Set up**
3. **Read the level.** `rms_dbfs` near -60 is a quiet room; speech is around -30 to -15. `-120` means silence from the driver, not a quiet room.
4. **Install it as a placed cog.** The host hands it the capture node and nothing else. → see **Set up**

You can test with no microphone: `--once --simulate` publishes a tone marked `SYNTHETIC`, and `--replay FILE` plays a recorded file through the same path.

## How the signal flows

```diagram
flow
```

## Honest limits

- It publishes what ALSA delivers. A card that cannot do 16 kHz mono natively is converted by ALSA's `plughw` layer.
- The stream is a ring in shared memory. A reader that falls behind loses chunks (the `seq` jumps); the writer never waits. A `block` reader is treated as `drop-oldest` by this writer.
- On a node where every cog runs under one user id, the node refuses a second claim on the microphone but cannot stop a cog from opening the device behind its back. The listing says `device_isolation: advisory`.
pages.troubleshoot:
# Troubleshoot

> What each failure looks like and what to do.

## `no_source`

The report's `error` says why.

| `error` starts with | Meaning | Do this |
|---|---|---|
| `no capture node in WEFTOS_DEVICES` | the host handed no capture node | place the cog through the controller, or pass `--device` |
| `no handed capture card matches` | the card name matches none of the handed cards | check `/proc/asound/cards` and the **Card name** setting |
| `arecord: ...` | `arecord` is missing | install alsa-utils |
| `the capture ended` | `arecord` exited | run `arecord -D plughw:1,0 -f S16_LE -r 16000 -c 1 -d 2 /tmp/t.wav` by hand and read its message |

## Level reads -120 dBFS

The device delivers digital silence: a muted capture control or the wrong card. Check `amixer -c 1 contents` and unmute capture.

## Level is high and `clipped_samples` grows

The report's `clipping` is true when more than 1% of chunks hold a clipped sample. The cog sets the card's capture level at start (**Capture level**, 50% by default) and applies **Software gain** (0 dB). Calibrated on the Ventuno's U20CAM with speech at about 1 m: 100% clipped 89 of 350 chunks; 70% peaked at -2.3 dBFS; 50% at -7 dBFS with no clipping; 20% at -14 dBFS. Lower **Capture level** for a louder room, raise it for a quiet or distant voice, or set it to `off` to leave the card alone. The setting stays on the card after the cog stops; restore it with `amixer -c <card> sset Mic 100%`.

## `bus.connected` is false

`bus.error` holds the broker's refusal. `unauthorized` or `unknown_topic` means the cog was placed without its `[[outputs]]`; place the package again.

## Chunks per second below 50

The reader of the pipe is starved. Look for a busy CPU; `short_reads` counts failed reads.

title = "Microphone capture on a Linux board"
